Vendored transpiled copy of jellyfin-plugin-media-bar slideshowpure.js, pinned upstream commit ae878fd763c1d2065db4dcbc7d15a90539a0f813, transpiled+minified with esbuild 0.21.5 --target=es2017 (lowers the optional chaining that makes the raw CDN copy die at parse on Tizen 5.0 / Chromium 63 / V8 6.3, blanking the home hero). Gate below: engines that can PARSE `?.` run the CDN copy untouched - this entry is a no-op there. Only parse-dead engines execute the vendored copy; the MediaBar inline WebConfig script polls for window.slideshowPure every 100ms, so late install still picks up server config. Regeneration recipe lives in docs/jela115-mediabar-tizen5-rescue.md. JELA-117/JELA-120: the two CONFIG.enableTrailers use-sites below carry an extra `jpQmNative()` guard (LOCAL EDIT vs upstream - keep it when regenerating): the YouTube embed player crashes without queueMicrotask (even its es5 build). The probe must test a FRESH IFRAME realm, not this window - Jellyfin's core-js polyfills queueMicrotask on the main window (so `typeof queueMicrotask` lies on M63, JELA-120), but the cross-origin YouTube embed document never loads that polyfill. Engines whose pristine iframe realm lacks native queueMicrotask (Tizen 5.0 / M63) get backdrop-only hero slides instead of a stalled dead trailer slide. JELA-257 (LOCAL EDIT vs upstream - keep when regenerating): initLoadingScreen only - #page-loader gets an absolute 15s fail-open (skipped if the loader is already gone) plus a 450ms fallback alongside the transitionend listener, so an unreachable youtube.com/iframe_api no longer leaves the black overlay covering a rendered home forever (the JELA-253 symptom). Boot still hard-waits on loadYouTubeAPI BY DESIGN: JELA-253's wider fail-open (onerror + 8s null resolve, boot skipping the YT await so slidesInit ran without window.YT) bisected to a hard renderer-main-thread wedge on first D-pad or pointer input on M63/Tizen (JELA-257) - do not reintroduce it. Without YT the hero simply stays absent and home is usable. JELA-286 (LOCAL EDIT - keep when regenerating): on engines whose pristine iframe realm lacks native queueMicrotask (jpQmNative() false - Tizen 5.0 / M63) the YT embed can never produce slides, so initLoadingScreen's home teardown no longer waits for #slides-container there - the loader clears as soon as .homeSectionsContainer exists instead of riding the 15s absolute fail-open, which stays as the last-resort backstop for unknown states. Slides still never mount without a real YT handle (JELA-257 rule intact). JELA-315 (LOCAL EDIT - keep when regenerating): sign-out teardown. SlideTimer callbacks self-stop when isUserLoggedIn() is false (kills orphaned timers a double loadSlideshowData init leaks - resetSlideshowState only stops the CURRENT reference), fetchItemDetails refuses falsy ids (no GET /Items/undefined ever), createSlideForItemId bails on a null item, updateVisibility clears the stale wasVisible latch + stops the timer when #slides-container left the DOM, loadSlideshowData stops any prior timer before reassigning, next/prevSlide no-op at totalItems 0. JELA-306: updateCurrentSlide guards the two unguarded derefs (slides container + target slide can be null after route/sign-out teardown lands during the createSlideForItemId await) and a try/finally clears the isTransitioning latch + restarts slideInterval on any bail/throw - one throw used to freeze the hero for the whole session. JELA-318 (LOCAL EDIT - keep when regenerating): initPageVisibilityHandler's pause/resume body is now a shared jpApply(), driven by visibilitychange AND by the window events jp:screensaver:shown / jp:screensaver:hidden that injector script #71 ambient-screensaver dispatches on mount and teardown. The in-app screensaver is an opaque full-screen overlay that the document visibility API knows nothing about, so before this the hero kept flipping and fetching item details behind it for the whole overnight idle. A body.jp-screensaver-active check backs the events up: it is consulted at install time and on visibilitychange, so a tab becoming visible under a live screensaver does not resume. CustomJavaScripts.Name: JellyPlug — notifysync-tizen5-rescue (RETIRED JELA-290)
CustomJavaScripts.Script:
/* JellyPlug - notifysync-tizen5-rescue: RETIRED 2026-08-03 (JELA-290).

   This slot carried a 31,519-byte vendored transpile of the NotifySync plugin
   client (/NotifySync/client.js, pinned V5.7.15.0, esbuild --target=es2017) so
   that Tizen 5.0 / Chromium 63 / V8 6.3 -- which cannot parse the `??` the
   plugin ships -- still got a notification bell.

   Retired because the bell it built could never be seen or opened. #41
   header-declutter hides every `.skinHeader .headerButton` whose material-icon
   ligature is `casino` or `notifications` unless the className matches #41's
   allow regex, and `netflix-bell` is NOT in that list -- only `jp-notif-bell`
   is. Measured live on Tizen 5.0 UA: `#netflix-bell` was `display:none`,
   `tabIndex:-1`, `offsetParent:null`, `aria-hidden="true"`,
   class `... jp-header-decluttered`. That is equally true of the PLUGIN's own
   bell on every modern client (its client.js builds the same id + the same
   `paper-icon-button-light headerButton headerButtonRight` + the same
   `material-icons notifications` span), so hiding it is a fleet-wide product
   decision, not a TV regression: the theme's notification UI is #42
   notifications-inbox (`jp-notif-bell`), which is route-gated only and runs on
   TV. So the weakest client in the fleet was parsing 31 KB, injecting
   `#notifysync-css`, registering two MutationObservers plus a 5-minute poll and
   WebSocket handlers, and making one authenticated GET /NotifySync/Data per
   boot, to build an element with `display:none`.

   Second reason: nothing regenerated the vendored copy when the plugin was
   upgraded. The server already served a "NOTIFYSYNC V5.7.19.0" header marker --
   four versions ahead; `filterOther`, "Other" and "Codec & Audio" were all
   present upstream and absent from the vendored bytes -- and that drift would
   have grown silently with every NotifySync release.

   Nothing else in the corpus referenced `netflix-bell`,
   `notification-dropdown`, `notify-backdrop` or
   `__JP_NOTIFYSYNC_TIZEN5_RESCUE__`: this slot was self-contained.

   Retired in place rather than deleted so script indices stay stable (the
   corpus md5 map is keyed on index; append new scripts at the END only).

   Known, accepted loss: on a parse-dead engine the NotifySync entry in the
   admin dashboard sidebar keeps its stock icon instead of the bell glyph this
   script used to swap in. Cosmetic, admin-only, TV-only.

   To bring it back you must do BOTH: (1) regenerate from the CURRENT plugin
   version with the `esbuild --target=es2017` recipe, and (2) add `netflix-bell`
   to #41's allow regex -- or the bell is invisible again. Pre-retirement bytes:
   _default/jela290/27-live.js; rollback config:
   _default/jela290/config-live-pre-jela290.json.

   `tools/lint_vendored_drift.py` now fails when any vendored plugin copy drifts
   from what the server serves, and fails if this slot regains executable code
   without being re-registered in tools/vendored-drift-contract.json. */

CustomJavaScripts.Script:
/* JellyPlug — PERMANENT tx-bundle repair seed. Hands every TV back to the
   JELA-833 coalesced tx-bundle path by writing "0" UNCONDITIONALLY.

   DO NOT DELETE THIS ENTRY. Disposition settled on JELA-836 (approved
   2026-09-02): "drop it once \"0\" has propagated" has no terminating
   condition. The JELA-824 emergency kill wrote "1" into each TV's
   localStorage and that value outlives this channel entry; the read site is
   opt-OUT (jellyfin.shell.txBundleDisabled === "1" kills) and ALSO ships
   inside two un-updatable vehicles — the legacy full WGT's baked
   shell.min.js and the HSB WGT's baked boot-shell.min.js fallback — so no
   shell release can retire the key on a fielded TV, and no fleet signal can
   prove propagation (the diag device id is minted per profile, so it can
   never say "this TV booted again"). This entry is the only repair channel,
   permanently. Cost to keep: 0.066% of public.js. Cost of dropping it one TV
   early: +62 requests / +26 KB on every cold boot of that TV, forever.
   Details: docs/jela836-txbundle-seed-disposition.md. jp824kill */
